notes: DOCUMENTED TARGET — NOT RECORDABLE (daemon_capability: incapable; driver_capability: gap:permission-approval). This spec states the arc the row asserts so a future re-assessment has something concrete to compare against; it is NOT expected to pass on aider as it stands, and it deliberately is not weakened to match what aider can do. THE ROW: two DISTINCT waiting episodes in one session — one raised by a mutating tool, one raised by a READ-ONLY tool — with the arc ready -> working -> waiting -> working -> waiting -> working -> ready and a final ready that survives a >=10s trailing idle. AGENT LAYER (satisfied): aider gates both classes through io.confirm_ask — read-only via check_for_file_mentions ("Add file to the chat?", coders/base_coder.py:1772) and check_for_urls ("Add URL to the chat?", base_coder.py:976, approval calls cmd_web = a web fetch); mutating via handle_shell_commands ("Run shell command?", base_coder.py:2456) and allowed_to_edit ("Create new file?" 2207 / "Allow edits to file that has not been added to the chat?" 2226). confirm_ask is a blocking stdin read, so the two gates are strictly sequential and cannot merge into one episode. The phase ORDER below (read-only then mutating) follows aider's own turn cycle — file mentions are scanned on the assistant reply, shell commands are offered after edits are applied — and is NOT part of the row's claim, which asserts only that each class produces its own episode. TRANSPORT LAYER (why this cannot pass): aider's Source is FilesUnderCWD{.aider.chat.history.md, RawLineParser} and the adapter declares no hooks. confirm_ask prints the question to the terminal and reads the answer from stdin; the only append_chat_history calls inside it fire AFTER the answer (the res=='d' blockquote, and the ConfirmGroup-preference user_input echo), so nothing marks the dialog OPENING. The transcript is not literally silent — confirm_ask calls tool_output(subject) before it blocks (io.py:850-857) and tool_output appends a blockquote (io.py:995-999), so a bare `> <filename>` / `> <command>` line IS written just before the dialog opens — but it rides the same channel as every other aider status line and carries no dialog marker, and for a gate with neither allow_never nor a ConfirmGroup (confirm_ask("Create new file?", base_coder.py:2207)) the ANSWER writes nothing at all, so the release edge has no trace whatsoever. The parser drops non-error blockquotes with a comment naming "confirmation prompts" explicitly, and its toolCall() emits ToolUses and ToolResultIDs in ONE event so no tool call is ever open — which disarms SignalOpenToolStalled, the one transcript-tier rule built for exactly this case. All five waiting rules in state_classifier.go:106-207 are therefore unreachable for aider. What a run would actually show is the INVERSION this row exists to catch: while confirm_ask blocks, the transcript is quiet, Parser.IdleFlush fires after aiderIdleTurnDoneAfter (1500ms) and synthesizes turn_done, and the session is reported READY while the user stares at the modal. DRIVER LAYER: driver-interactive.sh hard-codes --yes-always, which aider cannot negate (args.py:760 is action="store_true", not BooleanOptionalAction), so no dialog is ever raised under the current rig; and there is no keys/approval step to answer one (DRIVE_ELICITS="send slash wait_turn interrupt sleep"). VACUOUS-PASS WARNING for whoever revisits this: aider CAN reach waiting, but only through the trailing-question/cue text classifier (state_classifier.go:437, over LastAssistantText). Because the dialog leaves no trace whatsoever, ANY waiting an aider recording of this cell shows is by construction NOT the dialog. Do not accept two waiting episodes as evidence for this row without also showing which confirm_ask call produced each. SESSION IDENTITY (same as aider/basic-turn and aider/token-quota-exhausted): the transcript is per-cwd markdown, so the daemon keys the whole session by proc-<PID>; there is no transcript-UUID rollout session. session_birth anchors to recording start UNPINNED so a transient presession row cannot steal the birth, and every later phase chains off it.

text: The proc-<PID> session appears in ready within 2s of the aider REPL launching
The prompt that needs one read-only call and one mutating call drives ready -> working

The READ-ONLY gate opens (check_for_file_mentions "Add file to the chat?" / check_for_urls "Add URL to the chat?") and the session goes working -> waiting while the dialog is on screen. This is the episode the row adds; it must be its own episode, not folded into the mutating one
The user answers the read-only dialog; the session resumes waiting -> working

The MUTATING gate opens (handle_shell_commands "Run shell command?" / allowed_to_edit) and the session goes working -> waiting a SECOND time — a distinct episode, which is what proves the two tool classes are told apart
The user answers the mutating dialog; the session resumes waiting -> working and the turn continues
The turn completes back to ready — full arc ready -> working -> waiting -> working -> waiting -> working -> ready
The session is still ready after a >=10s trailing idle — it does not fall back to waiting once the last dialog closes
A single process_exited on the session at REPL teardown; the live state immediately before teardown is ready
